title: How Should Federal IT Resellers Choose an RFQ Platform?
summary: Six criteria for picking a platform that finds the RFQs you can quote and helps you answer them.
body_markdown:
**Quick answer:** A federal IT reseller should choose an RFQ platform based on four things: whether it covers the contract vehicles you actually hold, whether it filters out requests you can't quote, how fast it gets each RFQ to the right people, and how much of the quoting work it takes off your team. Broad "government contracting software" lists rank tools for every job. For a reseller, the job is narrower: see every eligible request for quotes (RFQ) and get a compliant quote out before it closes.


‍


## Why do resellers need different criteria?


Most federal software guides, including our own[buyer's guide to government contracting software](https://www.govly.com/blog/best-government-contracting-software) , cover many jobs at once: market research, capture, proposals, policy tracking. A value-added reseller (VAR) selling IT products lives in a different workflow. Most of its federal revenue runs through contract vehicles, where agencies send RFQs straight to vehicle holders and response windows are short.


Those requests mostly sit inside each vehicle's ordering system, not on SAM.gov, which we explain in[why contract vehicle RFQs don't appear on SAM.gov](https://www.govly.com/blog/contract-vehicle-rfqs-not-on-sam-gov) . The Army's system is a good example. The[Army CHESS site](https://chess.army.mil/Content/Page/CHESS_OVR) calls CHESS "the Army's designated Primary Source for commercial IT," and its[FAQ](https://chess.army.mil/Content/Page/FAQ) says Army regulations make it the mandatory source for commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) IT hardware, software and services. A platform that only watches SAM.gov will miss that whole stream.


‍


## What should a reseller look for in an RFQ platform?


Use these six criteria. The first two decide whether a tool is even in the running.


CriterionWhat to askWhy it matters for resellersVehicle coverageWhich ordering portals does it pull RFQs from, and how?If your vehicles aren't covered, the tool can't show you your own pipeline.Eligibility filteringCan it filter by vehicle, category or group, agency and product?Requests you can't quote waste the time you need for the ones you can.Routing and alertsDo alerts go to a team, and can different reps own different vehicles or agencies?Short windows punish an RFQ that sits in one person's inbox.Quote buildingCan it pull line items from quote documents and match your contract line items?Rekeying part numbers is where time and errors pile up.Partner sharingCan you share an RFQ with an original equipment manufacturer (OEM) or distributor without buying them a seat?Most reseller quotes depend on partner pricing and deal registration.SecurityWhat has the vendor's environment been assessed against?Defense customers may ask how your tools handle controlled unclassified information (CUI).


‍


## How do you test vehicle coverage?


Don't accept a logo slide. Bring a list of the vehicles you hold and ask the vendor to show live RFQs from each one, in a demo or a trial, against your own past requests if possible.


Ask how each source gets in. Some portals can be read directly. Others depend on a holder forwarding its RFQ emails into the platform. Forwarding-based coverage works, but only if your team keeps the forwarding rule in place, so you should know which kind each vehicle is.


Also check the transition cases. Vehicles turn over. NASA, for example,[is running SEWP V and SEWP VI concurrently](https://www.sewp.nasa.gov/) from November 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027. A good platform shows both and lets you filter one from the other.


‍


## Why does filtering matter so much?


Coverage without filtering just moves the firehose from your inbox to a new screen. A question resellers often raise in evaluations is why they're seeing RFQs they aren't eligible to quote.


Eligibility on a vehicle can depend on your category or group, the agency, set-asides and whether you carry the product line. Ask the vendor to show a saved search that narrows a busy vehicle to the requests one rep can actually answer. Then ask how a rep hides a request the team has passed on, so it doesn't keep coming back.


‍


## What separates quoting help from search?


Finding the RFQ is half the work. The other half is building a quote that matches your contract. On many vehicles, every item you quote has to exist as a contract line item, or CLIN (see[what a CLIN is](https://www.govly.com/blog/what-is-a-clin) ), and some vehicles require a catalog update before a new item can be quoted.


Ask the vendor to take one of your real quotes and show the steps: pulling line items out of a distributor's PDF or spreadsheet, matching them to your CLINs, and preparing any catalog update the vehicle requires. If each of those steps is still copy and paste, the platform is a search tool, not an RFQ tool.


‍


## Reseller evaluation checklist


- Bring your vehicle list and confirm live RFQs from each one.
- Ask which sources are read directly and which depend on email forwarding.
- Build one saved search per rep and check how much noise remains.
- Confirm alerts can go to a shared team, not only to individuals.
- Run one real past quote through the line-item and CLIN workflow.
- Share one RFQ with an OEM or distributor contact and see what they need to view it.
- Ask for the vendor's security assessment documentation.
- Ask which users need paid seats and which partners can view shared opportunities without one.


‍

## FAQ


**Should a reseller use separate tools for federal and state, local and education (SLED) bids?**
Not necessarily. If most of your state and local work comes through cooperative contracts or agency portals, a platform that covers both in one feed saves a second set of alerts and logins.


**How long should a trial last for a reseller?**
Long enough to see a full cycle of RFQs on your busiest vehicle, which for most resellers means a week or more of live requests.


**Who on a reseller team should own the platform?**
Usually whoever manages the contract vehicles, with sales reps owning their own saved searches, so coverage and catalog settings stay consistent.


**Does an RFQ platform replace a CRM?**
No. An RFQ platform finds requests and helps build quotes; a CRM tracks accounts and forecasts, and the two should pass opportunities back and forth.
